doc.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: Whiteman-band players on Bix and Berigan
summary: Charlie Margolis and Benny Baker called Bix and Bunny terrible; point of view.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: I actually don’t remember many people from that period, but I bet there were some great characters. I knew some of the — like Al Gallodoro and some of the people from that Whiteman band, later on I got to know, and Charlie Margolis was the first trumpet player. Charlie Margolis said, “Bix was terrible” you know. He says, “Well maybe Bix wasn’t a great section player. Charlie was a magnificent trumpet player, technically, wonderful. And another parallel example to that, there was a trumpet player from New York by the name of Benny Baker who played first trumpet under Toscanini, and everybody was studying from him at one time. And Doc Severinsen used to take his lesson ahead of me. He’d be in there playing those etudes like he owned them, and I’d go in and struggle. But the point to this whole thing is that Benny Baker also did commercial work as well as playing first trumpet in the orchestra. So he’d do radio, it was radio in those days. And they would give him section players like Bunny was on staff at CBS. He says, “Bunny was terrible.” © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
Oh isn’t that interesting. Depends on your outlook, doesn’t it.
It sure does. Your point of view.
